question.text: A proton is bombarded on a stationary lithium nucleus. As a result of the collision two <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi></math>-particles are produced. If the direction of motion of the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">α</mi></math>-particles with the initial direction of motion makes an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cos</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mfenced><mfrac bevelled="true"><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mfenced></math>, then the kinetic energy of the striking proton is [Given, binding energies per nucleon of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>Li</mi><mn>7</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math>  and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>He</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi>proton</mi></msub><mo>≈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi>neutron</mi></msub></math>]

solution.text:
Q value of the reaction is,

                                 Q = (2 × 4 × 7.06 – 7 × 5.6) MeV = 17.28 MeV



Applying conservation of energy for collision,

                                 Kp + Q = 2 Kα                 ....(i)

(Here, Kp and Kα are the kinetic energies of proton and α - particle respectively)

From the conservation of linear momentum (As there is no external force) ....(ii)

                               [Here P=2mk]
                                 ⇒ K⁡ p⁡ = 1 6 K⁡ α cos 2 θ = 1 6 K⁡ α 1 4 2 as m⁡ α = 4 m⁡ p⁡

∴                                 Kα =Kp                 ....(iii)

Solving eqs. (i) and (iii) with Q = 17.28 MeV


we get               Kp = 17.28 MeV
